body.p: I. Overview

Claims 1-20 are pending in the present application. Claims 1-3, 11-13 and 17 have been amended herein. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of the claims in view of the following amendments and remarks.
The issues raised by the Examiner in the current Office Action dated August 1, 2024 ("the Office Action") are as follows:
" Claims 1-20 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 101 because the claimed invention
is directed to non-statutory subject matter; and
" Claims 1-20 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over U.S.
Patent Publication No. 2022/0187912 to Alcaide.
Applicant respectfully traverses the outstanding claim rejections and requests reconsideration and withdrawal in light of the amendments and remarks presented herein.
II. Rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 101

Claims 1-20 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 101 as directed to non-statutory subject matter. Applicant disagrees that the Claims recite no more than mental steps. However, Applicant has amended the Claims to advance prosecution and to more clearly recite a technological improvement by which to evaluate and improve estimates of mental fatigue by a user of an IHS (Information Handling System, such as a laptop computer), where these estimates are generated based on physiological parameters collected by local sensors of the IHS and by remote sensors, such as wearable sensors. As amended, the Claims recite a non-generic computer improvement that utilizes sensor data and incorporates user input into a model of mental fatigue in the user's operation of the IHS, where the user input is solicited at the end of a break that has been detected between sessions of the user's operation of the IHS. See e.g., Specification, 0050. As such, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of the amended Claims.
III. Rejection of claims under 35 U.S.C. § 103

Independent Claim 1 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 based on Alcaide. Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection and provides amendments and remarks that clarify certain of the distinctions between the claimed invention and Alcaide, thus placing the Claims in condition for allowance over this reference.

Alcaide is deficient in many respects. The Claims recite: based on the monitored activity by the user and the monitored physiological parameters of the user, identify when the user stops operating the IHS and ends the first session. This does not appear present in Alcaide in any form. In Alcaide, a user is monitored during a session, but there does not appear to be any teaching or suggestion of detecting when a session ends.

This recited detection of a break between sessions is important because the Claims further recite: based on the monitored activity by the user and the monitored physiological parameters of the user, identify when the user resumes use of the IHS and begins a second session. This is also not present in any form in Alcaide.
Accordingly, Alcaide falls far short of disclosing what is claimed. Because the above

traversal applies equally with regard to independent Claims 1, 10 and 16, Applicant respectfully submits that all independent Claims are allowable. Applicant further submits that the dependent Claims are allowable for at least the same reasons as the independent claim from which each
depends. In view of the above traversal, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of these rejections and requests allowance of all Claims.
IV. Conclusion
Applicant has made a diligent effort to place the claims in condition for allowance.

However, should there remain unresolved issues that require adverse action, Applicant requests that the Examiner telephone Applicant's attorney at 512-582-2851 so that such issues may be resolved as expeditiously as possible.
